sub_questions.question: Why did the credit balance drop much faster this week despite no change in how the app is used?

claims.claim: Credits aren't charged at a flat rate per response.
claims.guide_evidence: Message credits are not consumed at a flat rate.

claims.claim: Lighter models can cost as little as 1 credit per response.
claims.guide_evidence: lighter models (for example smaller GPT variants) consume as little as 1 credit per response

claims.claim: Mid-tier models cost around 5 credits per response.
Heavier or multimodal models (transcription, text-to-speech, flagship chat) cost around 25 credits per response.
claims.guide_evidence: larger or multimodal models (audio transcription, text-to-speech, flagship chat models) around 10 credits per response

claims.claim: A shift toward heavier models in the mix could explain faster credit burn without any change in request volume.
claims.guide_evidence: A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster than the headline credit number suggests.

claims.claim: Checking usage logs for which model handled the most requests this week will confirm the cause.

customer_safety_issues: States a wrong credit cost (25 credits) for heavier models; the guide says around 10 credits.
evaluation.rationale: The answer gives the right general explanation (model mix drives variable credit cost). However, it contradicts the guide on the heavy-model rate: it says about 25 credits, but the guide says about 10. It also points the customer to "usage logs", which the guide never mentions. The wrong billing figure makes it unsafe to send as written.
